alarms.title: Shielding gas flow too low
alarms.operator_message: Gas flow is too low. The weld would get pores. The cell will not start welding.
alarms.technical_detail: Pre-purge flow measured 6 L/min against a minimum of 12 L/min (setpoint 15 L/min). Possible causes: cylinder nearly empty, valve partly closed, kinked hose, or spatter blocking the nozzle.

ground_truth.consequence_if_ignored: Porosity in the weld; part fails inspection.

expected_response.resolved_when: Gas check passes after the cylinder or hose problem is fixed.

hints: Low gas means the weld is not protected from air. Do not weld yet.
Look at the gas cylinder pressure, the valve, the hose and the nozzle.
Open the valve fully or change the cylinder, clean the nozzle, then press 'Check gas again'.

alarms.literature: Porosity from insufficient shielding: weld defects document; Zhang et al. 2026 (signal precursors of porosity).
resolution_script: Check the gas cylinder gauge. If it is near zero, change the cylinder.
Open the cylinder valve fully and check the hose for kinks.
Look into the nozzle. Remove spatter with the nozzle cleaner.
Press 'Check gas again'. Flow must be 12 L/min or more.
When the check is green, press 'Problem solved'.

alarms.title: Unstable arc: worn contact tip
alarms.operator_message: The arc was unstable for 7 seconds in the middle of the seam. Check that part of the weld.
alarms.technical_detail: Voltage standard deviation rose from 1.2 V to 4.8 V between 12 s and 19 s with frequent short-circuit bursts and wire-feed fluctuations, a pattern typical of a worn or spatter-blocked contact tip. The weld in that zone may show spatter and lack of fusion.

ground_truth.root_cause: Contact tip worn after many welds (simulated).
ground_truth.consequence_if_ignored: Next parts get the same spatter and fusion problems.

expected_response.resolved_when: Weld marked for inspection and contact tip change recorded.

hints: A jumpy arc usually comes from the torch, not from the settings.
Look at the contact tip: is the hole worn oval or full of spatter?
Mark this weld for inspection and change the contact tip before the next part.

alarms.literature: Electrical signals as arc-stability indicators: Geng et al. 2025; Zhang et al. 2026.
resolution_script: Open the replay at 12-19 s and look at the voltage line.
Mark this weld 'Check needed' for inspection.
Unlock the cell and stop the torch at the service position.
Remove the nozzle and the contact tip. A worn tip has an oval hole.
Fit a new contact tip, put the nozzle back, lock the cell.

alarms.title: Gap too wide: burn-through risk
alarms.operator_message: The gap between the parts is too wide at the end of the seam. The weld could burn through.
alarms.technical_detail: Seam scan shows the root gap growing from 0.8 mm to 2.4 mm over the last 60 mm. The preset procedure allows up to 1.5 mm on 3 mm plate. Fixed parameters cannot compensate for this gap.

ground_truth.root_cause: Part placed slightly rotated in holding robot B's gripper (simulated).
ground_truth.consequence_if_ignored: Burn-through or lack of fusion at the seam end.

expected_response.resolved_when: New seam scan shows the gap within 1.5 mm.

hints: A gap this wide on thin plate melts away instead of joining.
Check how the parts sit in the grippers at the end of the seam.
Let the robots put the parts down and pick them up again, then scan the seam again.

alarms.literature: Part dimension variation and fit-up as main problems of robotic welding: Curiel et al. 2023.
resolution_script: Do not weld: the gap is too wide for this plate.
Let robots A and B put the parts back in the stations.
Check that both parts sit flat and against the stops.
Let the robots pick the parts up again.
Run the seam scan again. The gap must be 1.5 mm or less.
If it is still too wide, set the part aside and press 'Problem solved' with a note.
